topicCandidates: Legal basis and route kind: activity-based status, status-or-position-based status, or an individually designated activity/program.
Official activity definition, positive activity examples, adjacent-status exclusions, and mixed or incidental duties.
Available periods of stay, program-wide aggregate limits, renewal/change availability, transition routes, and rules whose effective date matters.
Qualification pathways expressed as alternatives and conjunctions: relevant education, experience, recognized examinations, professional qualifications, language or skills tests, and exceptions.
Employer, contracting organization, host institution, business, remuneration, support-plan, family-relationship, nationality, and program conditions.
Work authorization boundaries: unrestricted work, status-limited work, no work by default, activities permitted outside status, and route-specific secondary activities.
Evidence categories and application context, separating entry/COE, change, extension, and post-grant notification requirements.
Source-level provenance, effective dates, review state, and uncertainty so the educational cross-reference uses only current reviewed assertions.
Cross-cutting travel and re-entry implications without duplicating the later dedicated re-entry guide.
School and institution classifications that affect Student, Professor, Instructor, Researcher, and related routes.
userSituations: A software developer checking whether actual duties, a related degree, experience, or a recognized IT examination can support Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services.
A private-language-school teacher, school teacher, and university instructor who share a job label but may fall under different residence statuses because the institution and activities differ.
A regulated professional whose degree or overseas license alone does not establish authority to perform work reserved to holders of a Japanese legal qualification.
A company founder comparing Business Manager with a local startup-preparation program and needing to distinguish entry preparation from operating an established business.
A sector worker comparing Specified Skilled Worker (i) and (ii), including tests, designated fields, family accompaniment, and aggregate stay limits.
A person with a family- or status-based residence status who can work without an immigration activity restriction but may still face licensing, employment, and tax rules.
A person shown only the label Designated Activities who must identify the individual designation before any duration, work, family, or renewal guidance can be reliable.

A resident considering freelance or side work whose proposed activity may be inside the current status, require individual permission, qualify for comprehensive permission, or require a status change.
A resident temporarily leaving Japan who must understand that re-entry permission and the underlying period of stay are separate clocks.
A prospective student comparing institution types whose admission rules and eligibility to support Student status are not interchangeable.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: Job title is not determinative; actual primary duties, contract, institution, and excluded activities control the status comparison.
A role can contain mixed duties. The model must distinguish principal, incidental, temporary-training, and outside-status activities rather than attach one occupation list to one status.

Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services includes distinct education/experience paths, a shorter experience path for some international-services work, a graduate exception for translation/interpreting/language instruction, and recognized IT examination or qualification exceptions.

A foreign vocational credential is not automatically equivalent to a qualifying Japanese professional-training-college title; credential type, country, curriculum, and route-specific rules must remain explicit.

Intra-company Transferee uses the same broad activity family as Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services but adds a corporate relationship, limited transfer period, designated workplace, and prior-service rule.

Legal/Accounting Services, Medical Services, and Nursing Care are license-dependent shapes; an academic credential and an immigration status do not replace the required Japanese professional qualification.
Highly Skilled Professional has activity subclasses, points or J-Skip paths, organization-linked activity, compound activities, and different transition timing for category 2.

Specified Skilled Worker varies by category and industrial field; tests, permitted tasks, Japanese level, support, family accompaniment, employer change, and aggregate duration cannot be stored as one status-wide sentence.
Business Manager criteria changed materially on 2025-10-16, so capital/investment, staffing, experience, language, office, and business-plan assertions require effective dates and transition notes.
Designated Activities is an envelope for many named and individually designated programs; program identity and the passport designation must be first-class, not a note under one generic route.
Status-based routes may have no immigration work restriction while regulated professions, employer policies, tax, and other laws continue to apply.
Permission to engage in activity outside the status may be comprehensive or individual and is not a reusable declaration that all side work is allowed.
The period requested, the period legally available, and the period actually granted are different; extension is discretionary and is not guaranteed by an available duration.
COE, visa issuance, landing permission, status of residence, and period of stay are separate decisions and must not share one eligibility field.
Special re-entry normally ends at the earlier of one year after departure and the current period-of-stay expiry; travel logic must reference, not overwrite, route duration.
Nationality, bilateral agreement, age, quota, and application-place constraints affect routes such as Working Holiday and some designated programs without applying to the whole status category.
Requirements and documents can differ for a first landing, COE, change of status, extension, employer change, and in-country acquisition.
Immigration approval does not decide professional licensing, employment-contract validity, tax treatment, or municipal obligations.
jurisdictionVariables: National immigration law, ministerial ordinances, notices, and Immigration Services Agency operational guidance.
Foreign ministry and consular visa procedure, including nationality-specific documentary practice, kept separate from residence-status eligibility.
Japanese professional regulators and competent ministries for licensed occupations.
Sector ministries and field-specific operational rules for Specified Skilled Worker and successor workforce programs.
Municipal startup-visa programs and local support organizations, within nationally authorized frameworks.
Education regulators, recognized institution lists, institution classification, and institution-specific admission rules.
Regional immigration bureau fact-finding and discretionary case assessment; local practice must not be presented as a different legal rule.

contentImpacts.reason: Pilot alternative qualification paths, recognized-IT exceptions, actual-duty examples, exclusions, remuneration, contracts, and mixed-duty cautions.
Pilot institution-controlled boundaries using teaching roles that cannot be classified by the word teacher alone.
Pilot a Japanese-professional-qualification-gated route and separation of immigration permission from licensing.
Pilot conjunctive business requirements, effective-dated reform assertions, and startup-program transitions.
Pilot category and sector variants, tests, support, family rules, and aggregate-duration constraints.
Pilot relationship-based eligibility and work-not-authorized-by-default behavior.
Pilot program identity and individualized designation instead of false status-wide requirements.
Pilot subclasses, point and J-Skip qualification paths, compound activities, and category transitions.
Consume structured primary-activity and outside-permission relationships without treating a status label as blanket approval.
Later implementation should consume status duration and exclusions while keeping re-entry as a separate cross-cutting procedure.
Later school discovery should consume institution classifications without conflating school admission with Student-status eligibility.

scopeBoundaries: Iteration 2B should implement a reusable data model and a representative internal/public pilot only; it should not populate every route or rewrite all visa articles.
The educational cross-reference may compare reviewed rule assertions and direct users to official checks, but it must not calculate or promise individual eligibility.
Occupation examples are discovery and search aids, never a whitelist; actual duties and all applicable conditions remain controlling.
Application-document inventories belong to later route research and should initially be modeled as evidence categories plus source links, not copied as universal checklists.
Re-entry details belong to Iterations 3A/3B or 4A/4B; Iteration 2B only ensures the status model can link to cross-cutting travel rules.
School-choice details belong to Iteration 4A/4B; Iteration 2B only represents institution types and institution-dependent activity boundaries needed by status comparisons.
Municipal startup programs, local procedures, tax, employment law, and professional licensing sources remain separate authorities even where the status record links to them.
No record may be marked editorially verified merely because it parses or cites a source; explicit human approval remains required.
unresolvedQuestions: Should the Iteration 2B public pilot expose all eight representative routes, or keep some fixtures internal until their article research batches are completed?
Should qualification logic use a small typed expression tree for allOf/anyOf/notApplicable, or typed pathway arrays with human-readable conditions and no executable eligibility semantics?
Should time-sensitive assertions carry effectiveFrom and effectiveTo at field level, or should all source-backed assertions use a generic validity window?
How much of the official occupation-code list should be retained as structured metadata versus later reviewed search terms and prose examples?
Should institution category be a shared taxonomy used by both residence-status and school records, even though school records are not implemented until Iteration 4B?
Should individually designated programs be child route records under Designated Activities or a separate program entity linked to the umbrella status?
Which evidence categories are stable enough for the pilot without implying that the list is complete for a nationality, employer category, or application context?
